title: Wrap content in Liquid Glass with NSGlassEffectView
summary: Use NSGlassEffectView to render a Liquid Glass background behind arbitrary content, with a configurable corner radius, tint, and style — the modern replacement for layering custom blur views.
pitfalls: Assign your view to contentView; do not addSubview directly — NSGlassEffectView manages its own content hierarchy.
Set cornerRadius on the glass view rather than clipping a wrapper layer, so the glass edge stays crisp.
replaces: manually layering NSVisualEffectView with custom CALayer blur
whenToUse: Reach for Liquid Glass on floating, content-forward surfaces (cards, panels, overlays) on macOS 26+. The HIG advises using glass to establish hierarchy without heavy chrome; avoid stacking glass on glass, which muddies legibility.

title: Concentric nested corners with NSViewCornerConfiguration
summary: Use NSView.cornerConfiguration with the containerConcentric radius so a nested view's corners stay visually concentric with its rounded container, instead of hardcoding a child radius.
pitfalls: effectiveCornerRadii is read-only — react to changes in viewDidChangeEffectiveCornerRadii, do not try to set it.
containerConcentric only resolves when an ancestor actually defines a corner radius; otherwise it falls back to zero.
replaces: hardcoding child corner radii that drift out of sync with the container
whenToUse: Use concentric corners whenever a control nests inside a rounded container (a glass card, a sidebar capsule) so the inner and outer curves share a center, which the HIG calls out as essential to a cohesive Liquid Glass look. Prefer it over fixed radii on macOS 27+.

title: View-based NSTableView with makeView + register cell reuse
summary: Drive a view-based NSTableView from a delegate that vends reusable NSTableCellView instances via makeView(withIdentifier:owner:), registering a nib or programmatic cell so rows recycle efficiently.
pitfalls: The identifier you pass to makeView must match the cell view's identifier, or reuse silently breaks and you allocate a new view every row.
Set the cell's textField outlet so NSTableCellView's built-in appearance updates (selection, backgroundStyle) work.
whenToUse: Use a view-based NSTableView for homogeneous, scrollable lists of records where each row is a lightweight cell; the HIG recommends tables for structured data the user scans or sorts. For richer grid layouts prefer NSCollectionView.

title: Sidebar/content/inspector layout with NSSplitViewController
summary: Compose a three-pane window — sidebar, content, inspector — with NSSplitViewController and dedicated sidebar/inspector split view items, getting collapsing, full-height layout, and toolbar integration for free.
pitfalls: Use the sidebarWithViewController: / inspectorWithViewController: initializers, not a plain item, so the panes get system sidebar material and the toggleSidebar toolbar wiring.
Pair allowsFullHeightLayout with NSToolbarItem.Identifier.sidebarTrackingSeparator to keep the toolbar divider aligned with the sidebar edge.
whenToUse: Use NSSplitViewController for the canonical macOS sidebar/content/inspector shell; the HIG describes the sidebar as the primary navigation surface for apps with distinct top-level sections. Prefer it over hand-rolled NSSplitView wiring.
